A write-ahead log is a file that contains a record of all changes made to the database. When a change is made to the database, the change is first written to the log, and then the change is written to the database itself. This ensures that the log always contains a complete and accurate record of all changes made to the database, even if the database itself is corrupted or lost.
When a database crashes, the write-ahead log can be used to recover the database to a consistent state. The log is scanned to determine the last consistent point in the database, and all changes made after that point are discarded. The database is then rebuilt from the log, using the changes that were made before the crash. This ensures that the database is recovered to a consistent state, with all changes that were made before the crash being preserved.
The write-ahead log also provides a way to recover from partial failures, such as a disk failure that causes some but not all of the database to be lost. In this case, the log can be used to recover the lost data, by replaying the changes that were made to the database before the failure. This ensures that the database is consistent and up-to-date, even if some changes were not fully written to the database before the crash.
The log can also be used to recover from a situation where the database is inconsistent, such as when a transaction is partially committed but not fully committed. In this case, the log can be used to determine which transactions were partially committed and which ones were not, and the database can be restored to a consistent state by rolling back the partially committed transactions.
In summary, a write-ahead log provides a way for a database to recover from crashes and inconsistencies by maintaining a complete and accurate record of all changes made to the database
